newsitem.title: HONG KONG: HK money rates steady to firmer in quiet trade.
newsitem.headline: HK money rates steady to firmer in quiet trade.

text.p: Interbank rates and government paper yields were firmer in very quiet trading on Monday as participants took a wait-and-see attitude on the first day of the Real Time Gross Settlement (RTGS) system, dealers said.
Overnight money rose to 5-1/4 1/8 from 5-1/8 five on Friday and three-month was little changed at 5-5/8 9/16.
"Market sentiment is a bit cautious with the start of the RTGS and the recent decline on U.S. long bonds," a European bank dealer said. U.S. Treasuries closed slightly down on Friday.
Dealers said there were no particular problems in the implementation of the RTGS system in the morning.
Dealers said short-term money rates should move slightly higher later this month due to the month- and year-end effect.
"Traders are not interested in offering long-term money, and short-term funds are largely centralised in the hands of the Hong Kong Monetary Authority," one dealer said.
Trading in government paper was thin with bill and note yields falling across the board.
One-week bill yields eased to 4.03 percent, down from 4.33 on Friday and one-month yielded 4.27 versus 4.34.
But demand was light as most traders already had prepared their positions for intraday repurchases, dealers said.
The three-year note yield was 6.02 percent against 6.08, the seven-year yielded 6.95 percent versus 6.99 and 10-year note yields fell seven basis points to 7.18.
